goal: Determine whether a control plane based on a pending sheet preserves the ledger's append-only discipline or introduces a parallel write path.
context: The ledger is only written after the human confirm, so a UI that reads only the ledger can never be the gate. The pending sheet is the proposed pre-confirm artifact. We need to know whether it creates a second source of truth. Outputs feed the Phase 2 decision.

groups.anti_bias: source of authority (ledger discipline vs control-plane practice)

agents.angle: defends the append-only invariant — looks for every path where the pending sheet becomes a parallel write
agents.initial_prompt: Survey how append-only systems handle pre-commit state. Does the pending sheet introduce a second source of truth? Return: concrete mechanisms with citations, or a defended no. Budget ~900 tokens.

agents.angle: defends control-plane ergonomics — looks for the cost of NOT having a pre-confirm artifact
agents.initial_prompt: Survey control-plane patterns with a human gate (staged changes, plan/apply, PR review). How does the pre-confirm artifact relate to the committed log? Return patterns with sources. Budget ~900 tokens.
Reconcile the explorers' returns into a candidate picture: every claim that bears weight cites the return it rests on. Budget ~2500 tokens.
Attack the synthesis. The strongest case that the pending sheet BREAKS the ledger discipline. Budget ~1200 tokens.
